Incident response team, we have a critical operational post-mortem and mitigation plan for the Kafka cluster partition leader rebalance failure during yesterday's traffic surge.

First, examine server.properties in the config directory to confirm that auto-leader-rebalance-enable is set to true and verify that leader-imbalance-per-broker-percentage is configured to 1%. Next, check kafka-core/partition_assignor.java in the kafka-core directory and inspect controller.py in the cluster-manager package. The primary root cause was an unexpected network partition between availability zones us-east-1a and us-east-1b causing 24 brokers to simultaneously trigger leader elections across 2,000 partitions. During the cascading election phase message production halted because min-insync-replicas was set to 3 while replica lag exceeded replica-lag-time-max-ms of 10,000 milliseconds. To remediate this cascade we must tune ZooKeeper session timeouts from 6 seconds to 30 seconds and adjust group-initial-rebalance-delay-ms from 3 seconds to 0 seconds for low-latency consumer group handoffs.

In addition, update controller.py to ensure that partition state machine transitions throttle concurrent leader reassignments to 50 partitions per second rather than unconstrained batch elections. Under no circumstances should any engineer modify the unclean-leader-election-enable setting to true as that would risk catastrophic data loss across financial audit logs. The principal systems architect requires that all broker nodes configure socket-send-buffer-bytes to 1 MB and socket-receive-buffer-bytes to 1 MB to prevent TCP buffer starvation under high load. Confirm that consumer applications utilizing the Java client library implement backoff retries using exponential jitter starting at 200 milliseconds capped at 5,000 milliseconds. Incident coordinators should also review the runbook in docs/runbooks/kafka_rebalance.md to verify that manual topic partition rebalancing commands specify explicit throttle rates.

Furthermore, the observability team must establish automated Grafana alerts triggered when under-replicated-partitions count exceeds 0 for more than three consecutive minutes. Also verify that all broker nodes emit JMX metrics to Datadog tracking active controller count and offline partition count with 0-second reporting intervals. The data platform engineering manager confirmed that all storage volumes must maintain 20% free disk space before resuming high-throughput bulk ingestion pipelines. Network engineers must inspect edge load balancers to ensure TCP keepalive probes are enabled with an interval of 30 seconds and probe count of 3. In addition, verify that consumer group heartbeat threads execute on dedicated high-priority CPU cores to avoid false positives during heavy garbage collection pauses.

The billing ingestion pipeline must also configure consumer max-poll-interval-ms to 300,000 milliseconds to accommodate long-running batch database transactions. Do not execute broker rolling restarts during peak business hours between 9:00 AM and 6:00 PM Eastern Time without vice president approval. All schema registry client libraries must enable local in-memory schema caching with a maximum capacity of 10,000 schemas to minimize HTTP request overhead. In addition, security operations must audit SSL certificate expiration dates across all broker nodes and ensure automated rotation 30 days prior to expiration. Site reliability engineers will execute simulated broker failure drills in staging next Tuesday morning to validate that partition rebalancing completes in under 45 seconds. The backup and disaster recovery team must confirm that MirrorMaker 2 replication lag between primary and secondary cloud regions remains below 2 seconds. Furthermore, log segment compaction threads must be configured with min-cleanable-dirty-ratio set to 0.5 to avoid excessive disk I/O during active hours.

Client application connection pools must enforce idle connection timeouts of 60 seconds to prune orphaned TCP sockets. The platform security team requires mutual TLS authentication between all producers and brokers using certificates issued by our internal Vault PKI. Incident leads must also ensure that post-incident action items are tracked in Jira with assigned engineering owners and target completion dates within two sprints. Regarding our upcoming migration to KRaft consensus architecture, please inspect kraft.properties in the metadata directory. Confirm that controller-quorum-voters lists all five dedicated KRaft controller nodes across independent rack topologies. Verify that metadata log replication segment size is configured to 64 MB and metadata snapshot interval is set to 1 hour. All transactional producer applications must enforce enable-idempotence set to true with transaction-timeout-ms configured to 30,000 milliseconds. In addition, the JVM runtime flags on all broker instances must pin the G1 garbage collector with max-gc-pause-millis set to 20 milliseconds and initiating-heap-occupancy-percent set to 45% to eliminate stop-the-world latency spikes during active partition movements. Tiered storage offloading must be enabled for all historical topic partitions older than 48 hours streaming compressed segments directly to encrypted S3 buckets. The data governance team mandates that topic deletion operations require dual authorization signatures in the cluster administration portal. Finally, schedule a comprehensive architectural readiness review for Friday morning at 10:00 AM with the infrastructure director to audit all verified configuration diffs and authorize rollout to the production cluster.

Hey team, here is the multi-service deployment coordination checklist for our major platform upgrade tonight:

1. Verify that all primary database migration scripts have executed cleanly on staging and confirm that replication lag remains below 5 seconds across all read replicas.
2. Drain incoming client traffic from the legacy v1 routing pool and redirect background worker queues to maintenance mode.
3. Deploy the new backend API container images to the secondary Kubernetes cluster and execute automated smoke testing suites against health endpoints.
4. Warm the distributed Redis cache cluster with pre-computed product catalog snapshots to eliminate database connection spikes during initial cutover.
5. Update global Route 53 latency routing policies to direct 10% canary traffic to the new cluster and observe error rates on Grafana for 15 minutes.
6. Complete the global traffic cutover to 100% on the new deployment after verifying that customer checkout error rates remain under 0.01%.
7. Notify technical customer support and partner engineering channels that the deployment has successfully stabilized.
8. Re-enable automated cron reconciliation jobs in the billing worker cluster after confirming that database write queues are clear.
9. Archive all pre-deployment database snapshots and diagnostic system traces to immutable S3 storage for audit compliance.
10. Conduct a 15-minute operational retrospective in the war room to verify that all metrics meet service level agreements.
11. Review error budgets across all payment microservices and confirm that zero critical incidents remain unacknowledged in PagerDuty.
12. Execute synthetic end-to-end checkout transactions across all supported international currencies to confirm payment gateway settlement.
13. Verify that search indexing clusters have synced all product catalog updates from the primary event bus without lag spikes.
14. Confirm that CDN edge distribution caches flush stale homepage assets and warm key localized landing pages.
15. Export final deployment metric dashboards and attach the operational sign-off report to the engineering wiki.
16. Audit security certificate expiration dates across all edge ingress load balancers and confirm that automated renewal hooks succeed.
17. Verify that canary analysis algorithms detect zero anomalous error spikes across all microservices before closing the deployment war room.

The release coordinator confirmed that if any step encounters unrecoverable errors, we must trigger the automated rollback script immediately. All on-call engineers must remain in the release Slack channel until the incident commander signs off on the deployment. Ensure customer billing statements generated during the cutover window are queued for secondary reconciliation tomorrow morning. Under no circumstances should any engineer execute manual hotfixes on production database primary nodes without incident commander sign-off.

Database operations team, here is the authoritative 26-step procedural runbook for tonight's cross-region PostgreSQL high availability switchover drill:

Prior to beginning the drill, verify that PostgreSQL query cancellation timeout is set to 15 minutes to avoid orphaned query transactions. The compliance director requires that PCI-DSS audit trails document all database administrative commands executed during maintenance. In addition, verify that `pg_stat_activity` shows zero active `idle in transaction` queries before initiating connection pool termination. The cloud networking team confirmed that cross-region Direct Connect latency between us-east and us-west averages 38 milliseconds. Finally, verify that the database standby instance has at least 64 GB of free RAM to accommodate sudden connection spikes upon traffic cutover.

1. Verify that replication lag between the primary cluster in us-east and the standby cluster in us-west is strictly below 100 milliseconds.
2. Verify disk space utilization across all database volumes in both regions remains strictly below 70%.
3. Post warning announcements to Slack channel incident management and join the mandatory war room Zoom bridge.
4. Redirect background read-only analytics queries to secondary read replicas to minimize lock contention.
5. Place the API gateway and client edge routers into read-only maintenance mode to prevent incoming write transactions during promotion.
6. Execute `SELECT pg_current_wal_lsn()` on the primary database node to record the authoritative cutover log sequence position.
7. Terminate active client backend connection pools using `pg_terminate_backend` on all application connections in us-east.
8. Execute `CHECKPOINT` on the primary instance to flush all dirty shared memory buffers to persistent NVMe disk volumes.
9. Verify that the us-west standby replica has received and replayed WAL through the recorded cutover LSN without gap anomalies.
10. Execute `pg_promote` on the target standby node in us-west and confirm that `pg_is_in_recovery()` returns false within 5 seconds.
11. Update Route 53 internal database DNS records to point `primary.db.enterprise.internal` to the promoted us-west endpoint.
12. Reconfigure Pgpool and PgBouncer connection poolers with new upstream host addresses and reload connection listener sockets.
13. Execute automated synthetic health check transactions on the promoted master to verify insert, update, and delete latency remains under 10 milliseconds.
14. Disable read-only maintenance mode on the edge API gateways and restore production application traffic to 100%.
15. Re-establish reverse streaming replication from us-west to us-east using `pg_basebackup` or `pg_rewind` to maintain secondary disaster recovery posture.
16. Monitor Grafana dashboards for 30 minutes tracking replication lag, connection pool utilization, and query error rates.
17. Verify that automated database snapshot schedules in AWS RDS or Aurora are re-synchronized across the promoted cluster.
18. Ensure that Postgres VACUUM background workers resume table statistics maintenance after promotion without causing I/O saturation.
19. Archive all pre-switchover diagnostic log bundles and WAL timeline history files to immutable S3 compliance buckets.
20. Conduct a 15-minute team debrief in the database Slack channel to document lessons learned and approve ticket closure.
21. Verify that application connection pool latency drops below 5 milliseconds on the promoted primary node.
22. Verify that read replica lag across all secondary regions remains strictly below 50 milliseconds.
23. Re-enable automated cron maintenance jobs and vacuum scheduler workers on the primary database node.
24. Execute security compliance checks verifying that database encryption at rest remains enabled with AWS KMS keys.
25. Notify the incident commander and engineering executive leadership via PagerDuty that failover completed successfully.
26. Close the change management ticket in ServiceNow with attached execution logs and performance graphs.

The incident commander confirmed that if replication replay stalls for more than 60 seconds during step 9, we must abort the promotion and revert gateway traffic immediately. All participating database administrators and SRE engineers must remain connected to the primary Zoom bridge until post-failover sign-off is completed. Under no circumstances should any engineer modify pg_hba.conf to allow unauthenticated database connections during the failover transition. Under no circumstances should any engineer restart database services during active WAL replay without explicit approval from the incident commander. The compliance director mandates that full failover timeline audit logs be attached to the change management ticket within 24 hours. The security operations center must be notified immediately once production database traffic is restored to regular operations. The lead database architect confirmed that max connections on PgBouncer must be configured to 2,000 connections with pool mode set to transaction. Furthermore, verify that Postgres connection poolers set max connections to 2,000 and idle connection timeout to 30 seconds. The site reliability team requires that Grafana alerts for replication lag exceed a threshold of 100 milliseconds for three consecutive checks. In addition, verify that database disk queue depth remains below 2 throughout the entire cutover window. The storage reliability team mandates that snapshot backups be triggered immediately after reverse streaming replication establishes clean sync. Moreover, verify that Prometheus node exporter metrics for memory swap utilization remain at 0% on all database host servers. Finally, verify that `pg_stat_statements` query execution statistics are reset to establish a baseline performance on the promoted master node.
